```{r}
to_sentence_oxford <- function(x) {
  n <- length(x)
  if (n == 0) return("")
  if (n == 1) return(x)
  if (n == 2) return(paste(x, collapse = " and "))
  paste(paste(x[-n], collapse = ", "), ", and ", x[n], sep = "")
}

vitamin_range_to_text <- function(r) {
  ranges <- c("min", "max")
  txt <- ""
  min <- dose_ranges[[paste0("min_d.", r)]]
  max <- dose_ranges[[paste0("max_d.", r)]]
  
  if (min == max) {
    txt <- glue::glue("the total daily dose was {min}")
    
  } else {
    txt <- glue::glue("the total daily dose ranged from {min} to {max}")
  }
 
  return(txt)
}

vitamin_duration_to_text <- function(r) {
  txt <- ""
  min <- duration %>% filter(grepl(glue::glue("{r}(?![0-9])"), intervention, perl = TRUE)) %>% select(duration) %>% min()
  max <- duration %>% filter(grepl(glue::glue("{r}(?![0-9])"), intervention, perl = TRUE)) %>% select(duration) %>% max()
  
  min_unit <- max_unit <- " weeks"
  if(min == 52) {
    min <- min/52
    min_unit <- " year"
  }
  if(min > 52) {
    min <- min/52
    min_unit <- " years"
  }
  if(max == 52) {
    max <- max/52
    max_unit <- " year"
  }
  if(max > 52) {
    max <- max/52
    max_unit <- " years"
  }
  
  if(min_unit == max_unit) {
    min_unit <- ""
  }
  
  if (min == max) {
    txt <- glue::glue("and the duration of supplementation was {max}{max_unit}")
    
  } else {
    txt <- glue::glue("and the duration of supplementation ranged from {min}{min_unit} to {max}{max_unit}")
  }
 
  return(txt)
}
```

```{r}
  select(-study, -bias.overall) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "domain",

  ) %>%
  filter(judgment != "low") %>%

  summarize(n = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = n, n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(domain = forcats::fct_recode(domain %>% as.factor(),
                               "Random sequence generation" = "bias.sequence",
                               "Allocation concealment" = "bias.concealment",
                               "Blinding of participants and personnel" = "bias.blinding.participants",
                               "Blinding of outcome assessment" = "bias.blinding.outcome",
                               "Incomplete outcome data" = "bias.incomplete.outcome",
                               "Selective outcome reporting" = "bias.selective.outcome",
                               "Other sources of bias" = "bias.other"
    )) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n)) %>% 
  slice(1) %>% pull(domain)
```

## Study Selection {#sec-study-selection}

Using the prespecified selection criteria, we identified `r prisma_data$N_initial_studies` records. After removal of `r prisma_data$N_exclude` duplicates, `r prisma_data$N_screened` records underwent title and abstract screening, of which `r prisma_data$N_exclude_screen` were excluded for not meeting eligibility criteria. We then assessed `r prisma_data$N_full_text` full-text articles for eligibility and excluded `r prisma_data$N_exclude_full_text` because of an ineligible intervention, unavailable full text, use of a non-validated measure of depression or anxiety, duplicate data, or inadequate reporting for analysis. The remaining `r prisma_data$N_extracted` studies underwent data extraction and full eligibility review; `r prisma_data$N_exclude_after_extract` were subsequently excluded because they did not meet inclusion criteria or lacked usable quantitative outcome data. This left `r prisma_data$N_included` studies for inclusion in the review. Of these, `r prisma_data$N_main_analysis` low-risk-of-bias studies were included in the primary analysis, and `r prisma_data$N_sensitivity_only` additional eligible studies were retained for sensitivity analyses only. The study selection process is shown in the PRISMA flow diagram (@fig-prisma).

::: {#fig-prisma fig-cap="PRISMA Flow Diagram"}

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="8.5in"}
  knitr::include_graphics("../overall/jpeg/prisma_flow_diagram.jpeg")
} else {
  knitr::include_graphics("../overall/pdf/prisma_flow_diagram.pdf")
}
```

## Characteristics of Included Studies {#sec-results-characteristics}

The `r prisma_data$N_included` included studies were published between `r min(data$year, na.rm = TRUE)` and `r max(data$year, na.rm = TRUE)`. Interventions included B vitamins (`r n_tx_summary$N_B` studies), vitamin C (`r n_tx_summary$N_C`), vitamin D (`r n_tx_summary$N_D`), zinc (`r n_tx_summary$N_zinc`), magnesium (`r n_tx_summary$N_mag`), selenium (`r n_tx_summary$N_selenium`), iron (`r n_tx_summary$N_iron`), and multi-nutrient combinations (`r n_tx_summary$N_multi`). These categories were not mutually exclusive because some studies evaluated combination products containing more than one eligible micronutrient. `r n_tx_summary$N_antidepressant %>% english::Words()` studies evaluated micronutrients as adjuncts to antidepressant treatment. Follow-up ranged from `r min(data$duration, na.rm = TRUE)` weeks to `r sprintf("%.1f", max(data$duration, na.rm = TRUE)/52)` years (median: `r median(data %>% distinct(study, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(duration), na.rm = TRUE)` weeks). Most studies assessed depressive symptoms (n = `r n_depression`; `r round(n_depression/prisma_data$N_included * 100, digits = 1)`%), whereas fewer assessed anxiety symptoms (n = `r n_anxiety`; `r round(n_anxiety/prisma_data$N_included * 100, digits = 1)`%).

Among the `r data %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% distinct(study) %>% nrow()` low-risk-of-bias studies included in the primary analysis, `r n_tx_summary_low$N_B` evaluated B vitamins, `r n_tx_summary_low$N_C` vitamin C, `r n_tx_summary_low$N_D` vitamin D, `r n_tx_summary_low$N_zinc` zinc, `r n_tx_summary_low$N_mag` magnesium, `r n_tx_summary_low$N_selenium` selenium, and `r n_tx_summary_low$N_iron` iron, with `r n_tx_summary_low$N_multi` studies evaluating multi-nutrient combinations. As above, these categories overlapped because some trials included combination interventions. Follow-up ranged from `r min(data %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% pull(duration), na.rm = TRUE)` weeks to `r {mdd <- max(data %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% pull(duration), na.rm = TRUE)/52; if (mdd == as.integer(mdd)) sprintf("%.0f", mdd) else sprintf("%.1f", mdd)}` years (median: `r median(data %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% distinct(study, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(duration), na.rm = TRUE)` weeks). All `r n_depression_low` studies assessed depressive symptoms, and `r n_anxiety_low` (`r round(n_anxiety_low/(data %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% distinct(study) %>% nrow()) * 100)`%) also assessed anxiety symptoms. Additional study characteristics are shown in the Appendix.

## Population Characteristics {#sec-population-characteristics}

Overall, `r sum(data %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(baseline.N)) %>% format(big.mark = ",")` participants were included, with study sample sizes ranging from `r min(data %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(baseline.N), na.rm = TRUE) %>% format(big.mark = ",")` to `r max(data %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(baseline.N), na.rm = TRUE) %>% format(big.mark = ",")`. Of these, `r sum(data %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(baseline.N)) %>% format(big.mark = ",")` were from low risk-of-bias studies. A total of `r sum(data %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(final.N)) %>% format(big.mark = ",")` participants completed follow-up, corresponding to an overall attrition rate of `r sprintf("%.1f", (1 - (sum(data %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(final.N)) / sum(data %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(baseline.N)))) * 100)`%.

Among the studies in the primary analysis, `r sum(data %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(final.N)) %>% format(big.mark = ",")` participants completed follow-up, with study-level completer samples ranging from `r min(data %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(final.N), na.rm = TRUE) %>% format(big.mark = ",")` to `r max(data %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(final.N), na.rm = TRUE) %>% format(big.mark = ",")` and an overall attrition rate of `r sprintf("%.1f", (1 - (sum(data %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(final.N)) / sum(data %>% filter(bias == "low") %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(baseline.N)))) * 100)`%. These studies were more likely to account for missing data, most commonly using last observation carried forward; none used multiple imputation. In these studies, the mean age was `r sprintf("%.2f", weighted.mean(age_low$age, age_low$baseline.N, na.rm = TRUE))` years (range: `r min(age_low$age, na.rm = TRUE)`–`r max(age_low$age, na.rm = TRUE)`), and `r sprintf("%.1f", weighted.mean(male_low$male, male_low$baseline.N, na.rm = TRUE))`% of participants were male.

Across all studies (n = `r prisma_data$N_include`), `r round(nrow(measured %>% filter(total_obs > 0))) %>% as.integer()` (`r round(nrow(measured %>% filter(total_obs > 0))/nrow(measured) * 100)`%) reported at least one baseline micronutrient level. Among low risk-of-bias studies, `r nrow(measured_low %>% filter(total_obs > 0))` (`r round(nrow(measured_low %>% filter(total_obs > 0))/nrow(measured_low) * 100)`%) reported baseline levels; `r nrow(measured_low %>% filter(total_obs == 1))` (`r round(nrow(measured_low %>% filter(total_obs == 1))/nrow(measured_low) * 100)`%) measured one micronutrient and `r nrow(measured_low %>% filter(total_obs >= 2))` measured two.
Among low risk-of-bias studies, weighted mean baseline concentrations were: vitamin B9 `r vit_levels_low %>% summarize(weighted.mean(baseline.B9, baseline.N, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% pull() %>% vit$numeric_convert_vitamin_from_molar("vitamin B9",.)`, red blood cell B9 `r vit_levels_low %>% summarize(weighted.mean(baseline.rbc.B9, baseline.N, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% pull() %>% vit$numeric_convert_vitamin_from_molar("rbc.B9",.)`, vitamin B12 `r vit_levels_low %>% summarize(weighted.mean(baseline.B12, baseline.N, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% pull() %>% vit$numeric_convert_vitamin_from_molar("vitamin B12",.)`, vitamin D `r vit_levels_low %>% summarize(weighted.mean(baseline.D, baseline.N, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% pull() %>% vit$numeric_convert_vitamin_from_molar("vitamin D",.)`, zinc `r vit_levels_low %>% summarize(weighted.mean(baseline.zinc, baseline.N, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% pull() %>% vit$numeric_convert_vitamin_from_molar("zinc",.)`, magnesium `r vit_levels_low %>% summarize(weighted.mean(baseline.magnesium, baseline.N, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% pull() %>% vit$numeric_convert_vitamin_from_molar("magnesium",.)`, selenium `r vit_levels_low %>% summarize(weighted.mean(baseline.selenium, baseline.N, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% pull() %>% vit$numeric_convert_vitamin_from_molar("selenium",.)`, and ferritin `r vit_levels_low %>% summarize(weighted.mean(baseline.ferritin, baseline.N, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% pull() %>% vit$numeric_convert_vitamin_from_molar("ferritin",.)`.

Vitamins B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B7, and C were not measured in low risk-of-bias studies, either because baseline levels were not assessed or because measurements occurred only in studies excluded from the main analysis due to higher risk of bias.

Sex distribution and baseline clinical status varied across comparisons, with some interventions evaluated primarily in female or clinically depressed populations. The distribution of key study-level characteristics across the network is summarized in the Appendix (Appendix ##).

## Intervention Characteristics {#sec-intervention-characteristics}

Vitamin D (`r n_tx_summary_low$N_D` studies) was the most common intervention aside from placebo (`r vitamin_range_to_text('D')`; `r vitamin_duration_to_text('D')`).

B vitamins (`r n_tx_summary_low$N_B` studies) included B1 (`r vitamin_range_to_text('B1')`; `r vitamin_duration_to_text('B1')`), B6 (`r vitamin_range_to_text('B6')`; `r vitamin_duration_to_text('B6')`), B9 (`r vitamin_range_to_text('B9')`; `r vitamin_duration_to_text('B9')`), and B12 (`r vitamin_range_to_text('B12')`; `r vitamin_duration_to_text('B12')`).

Vitamin C (`r n_tx_summary_low$N_C` study) was evaluated at `r vitamin_range_to_text('C')` for `r vitamin_duration_to_text('C')`.

Minerals included zinc (`r n_tx_summary_low$N_zinc`; `r vitamin_range_to_text('zinc')`; `r vitamin_duration_to_text('zinc')`), magnesium (`r n_tx_summary_low$N_mag`; `r vitamin_range_to_text('magnesium')`; `r vitamin_duration_to_text('magnesium')`), selenium (`r n_tx_summary_low$N_selenium`; `r vitamin_range_to_text('selenium')`; `r vitamin_duration_to_text('selenium')`), and iron (`r n_tx_summary_low$N_iron`; `r vitamin_range_to_text('iron')`; `r vitamin_duration_to_text('iron')`). 

`r n_tx_summary_low$N_multi` studies evaluated multi-nutrient combinations, most commonly `r to_sentence_oxford(stringr::str_split(most_common_multi,",") %>% unlist())`.

## Risk of Bias Within Studies {#sec-results-rob}

`r sum("low" == qual$bias.overall)` studies were rated low risk (`r glue::glue("{round(mean('low' == qual$bias.overall) * 100, digits = 2)}%")`), `r sum("some concerns" == qual$bias.overall)` had unclear risk (`r glue::glue("{round(mean('some concerns' == qual$bias.overall) * 100, digits = 2)}%")`), and `r sum("high" == qual$bias.overall)` were high risk of bias (`r glue::glue("{round(mean('high' == qual$bias.overall) * 100, digits = 2)}%")`). The most frequent source of bias was `r most_common_bias %>% stringr::str_to_lower()`. Primary analyses were restricted to low risk-of-bias studies that had usable data. Two low-risk-of-bias studies only had interventions comparing dosing of the same micronutrient and were thus only analyzed in the sensitivity analyses. Domain-level assessments are shown in @fig-rob.

::: {#fig-rob}

![](../overall/pdf/rob.pdf){width=8.5in}

Risk of bias by domain. Studies were assessed by the Risk of Bias 1 tool.
:::

## Effect of Micronutrient Supplementation on Depression Symptoms {#sec-results-depression}

In analyses restricted to studies at low overall risk of bias, only vitamin D and selenium yielded posterior mean estimates with 95% credible intervals excluding the null (@fig-tx).

For vitamin D, the posterior mean effect was `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2) %>% as.numeric()` standard deviations compared with placebo (95% CrI, `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2) %>% as.numeric()` to `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2) %>% as.numeric()`). For context, assuming a standard deviation of approximately 9 points on the Beck Depression Inventory, this corresponds to roughly a 3-point greater improvement relative to placebo; because multiple depression scales were used across studies, this translation is intended as an illustrative approximation.

The posterior mean effect for selenium was larger in magnitude (SMD: `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)`; 95% CrI: `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`), but this estimate was informed by only `r data %>% filter(intervention == "selenium" & bias == "low" & target == "depression") %>% nrow()` studies (N = `r (data %>% filter(study %in% (data %>% filter(intervention == "selenium" & bias == "low" & target == "depression") %>% pull(study))) %>% distinct(study, intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% pull(baseline.N)) %>% sum()`) and should be regarded as preliminary.

Other micronutrients, including vitamin B6 (SMD: `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "B6") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)`, 95% CrI: `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "B6") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "B6") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`) and vitamin B1 (SMD: `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "B1") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)`, 95% CrI: `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "B1") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "B1") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`), showed point estimates suggestive of benefit, but credible intervals were wide and included the null (@fig-tx). CINeMA ratings indicated low confidence for selenium and very low confidence for all other comparisons (see Appendix).

Between-study heterogeneity was substantial: the posterior mean of $\tau$ was `r fit_dep %>% posterior::as_draws_df(variable = "tau")  %>% summary() %>% select(mean) %>% round(digits = 2)` (95% CrI: `r fit_dep %>% posterior::as_draws_df(variable = "tau")  %>% summarize_draws(~quantile(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))) %>% select('2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r fit_dep %>% posterior::as_draws_df(variable = "tau")  %>% summarize_draws(~quantile(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))) %>% select('97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`), comparable in magnitude to some estimated treatment effects.

Given the uneven distribution of baseline deficiency and depression status across interventions, subgroup and meta-regression analyses were conducted to evaluate potential effect modification. In meta-regression models, baseline deficiency and baseline depression were associated with larger estimated effects of vitamin D. Among populations that were both depressed and vitamin D deficient, the posterior mean effect was `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "yes", depressed == "yes") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)` (95% CrI: `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "yes", depressed == "yes") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "yes", depressed == "yes") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`). In depressed but non-deficient populations, the estimate was similar in magnitude but more uncertain (`r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "no", depressed == "yes") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)`, 95% CrI: `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "no", depressed == "yes") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "no", depressed == "yes") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`). In depressed populations with unknown deficiency status, the posterior mean effect was `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "NA", depressed == "yes") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)` (95% CrI: `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "NA", depressed == "yes") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "NA", depressed == "yes") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`). In non-depressed populations, estimated effects were close to null regardless of deficiency status. CINeMA ratings for vitamin D estimates for depressed populations were rated as low confidence while those in non-depressed populations were rated as very low confidence (see the appendix).

For selenium, subgroup estimates were based on minimal data. In a deficient, non-depressed population (one study), the posterior mean effect was `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium", def == "yes", depressed == "no") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)` (95% CrI: `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium", def == "yes", depressed == "no") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium", def == "yes", depressed == "no") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`). This estimate was rated as moderate confidence following the CINeMA guidelines. In a depressed population with unknown deficiency status (one study), the estimate was `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium", def == "NA", depressed == "yes") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)` (95% CrI: `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium", def == "NA", depressed == "yes") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r def_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium", def == "NA", depressed == "yes") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`). This estimate was rated as very low confidence following CINeMA guidelines. Results for other vitamins are provided in the Appendix.

Dose–response analyses suggested a possible gradient for vitamin D, although credible intervals overlapped across dose categories. For doses <1000 IU/day, the mean difference was `r dose_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", .dose == "<1000 IU") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)` (95% CrI: `r dose_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", .dose == "<1000 IU") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r dose_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", .dose == "<1000 IU") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`), compared with `r dose_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", .dose == "1000-3000 IU") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)` and `r dose_dep_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", .dose == ">3000 IU") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)` at higher dose categories (full estimates in Appendix).
Longer study duration was generally associated with attenuation toward the null, though estimates were imprecise. Vitamin D effects were largest in studies ≤8 weeks and diminished in longer-duration categories (see Sensitivity Analyses for full estimates).

In low risk-of-bias analyses, antidepressant augmentation trials formed a disconnected sub-network and were therefore modeled separately, with antidepressant monotherapy as the reference. These estimates did not contribute to indirect comparisons in the primary network. Augmentation effects were similar in magnitude to antidepressant monotherapy but were based on few studies. For example, only `r data %>% filter(intervention == "antidepressant, D" & target == "depression") %>% nrow()` studies evaluated vitamin D augmentation (SMD: `r ssri_results %>% filter(.trt == "Antidepressant, D") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)`, 95% CrI: `r ssri_results %>% filter(.trt == "Antidepressant, D") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r ssri_results %>% filter(.trt == "Antidepressant, D") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`), while `r data %>% filter(intervention == "antidepressant, B9" & target == "depression" & bias == "low") %>% nrow()` studies examined antidepressants plus vitamin B9 (SMD: `r ssri_results %>% filter(.trt == "Antidepressant, B9") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)`, 95% CrI: `r ssri_results %>% filter(.trt == "Antidepressant, B9") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r ssri_results %>% filter(.trt == "Antidepressant, B9") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`). Similarly, `r data %>% filter(intervention == "antidepressant, B12, B6, B9" & target == "depression" & bias == "low") %>% nrow()` study examined antidepressants plus vitamin B6, B9, and B12 (SMD: `r ssri_results %>% filter(.trt == "Antidepressant, B12, B6, B9") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)`, 95% CrI: `r ssri_results %>% filter(.trt == "Antidepressant, B12, B6, B9") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r ssri_results %>% filter(.trt == "Antidepressant, B12, B6, B9") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`).

## Effect of Micronutrient Supplementation on Anxiety Symptoms {#sec-results-anxiety}

Among studies at low overall risk of bias, no examined vitamins or minerals had 95% credible intervals excluding the null. The largest estimated effect was observed for selenium (SMD `r anx_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)`, 95% CrI: `r anx_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r anx_results %>% filter(.trt == "Selenium") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`); in contrast to its effect on depression, vitamin D was estimated to have little average effect on anxiety symptoms. Only one low risk-of-bias study evaluated antidepressant augmentation with vitamin D for anxiety, so this estimate is not presented. All estimates were rated as very low confidence according to CINeMA guidelines (see the appendix).

The posterior mean of $\tau$ in the anxiety network was `r fit_anx %>% posterior::as_draws_df(variable = "tau")  %>% summary() %>% select(mean) %>% round(digits = 2)` (95% CrI: `r fit_anx %>% posterior::as_draws_df(variable = "tau")  %>% summarize_draws(~quantile(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))) %>% select('2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r fit_anx %>% posterior::as_draws_df(variable = "tau")  %>% summarize_draws(~quantile(.x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))) %>% select('97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`). Despite largely null effects, heterogeneity was substantial.

Subgroup estimates stratified by baseline deficiency and baseline anxiety status likewise yielded no comparisons with credible intervals excluding the null. For vitamin D, the posterior mean effect in deficient populations with baseline anxiety was `r def_anx_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "yes", anxiety == "yes") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)` (95% CrI: `r def_anx_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "yes", anxiety == "yes") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r def_anx_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "yes", anxiety == "yes") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`), and in non-deficient populations with baseline anxiety was `r def_anx_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "no", anxiety == "yes") %>% pull(Estimate) %>% round(digits = 2)` (95% CrI: `r def_anx_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "no", anxiety == "yes") %>% pull('q2.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)` to `r def_anx_results %>% filter(.trt == "D", def == "no", anxiety == "yes") %>% pull('q97.5%') %>% round(digits = 2)`). No studies assessed vitamin D for anxiety in populations with unknown deficiency status. Results for other micronutrients are provided in the Appendix. No clear patterns emerged in duration- or dose-stratified analyses for anxiety outcomes (Appendix).

No clear patterns were observed in duration- or dose-stratified analyses (Appendix).
